title: The design step is staffed between Gate 1 and the plan, and is skippable
description:
SPIDR child 2 of task-8a6d6660c31c4e119f962d13e6f1505d (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). dependsOn child 1 task-5e90317e80ac4b86a9704b6b8ba8874a for the kinds and aggregate.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the LOOP change. The affordance surface offers a design step after Gate 1 and before decomposition; the wrapper staffs a design seat with a mission that reads the approved contract and the PRD; the compiler mission then carries the design ref and its section headings; node missions cite the screens/entities they implement; and a per-goal toggle skips the whole step. No UI - that is child 3.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb:
- The compiler seat plans straight from the approved contract today: `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-mission-text.ts` `compilerMission` (:78) tells the seat to read `product_contract_read` and the paged PRD and submit the decomposition. There is no design in the chain.
- The affordance surface composes steps in `apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts`; a new step kind joins that composition.
- The wrapper staffs any READY unclaimed step up to maxAgents (`agent-wrapper.ts:339-372`), skipping HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS (:351) and `session.*` kinds, ordering `node.deliver` first (:348-357) - a design step must fall out of that ordering sensibly rather than competing with node work.

THE SKIP TOGGLE IS A SAFETY VALVE, not a nicety: the parent's DoD 4 requires that a goal can plan WITHOUT a design so the loop never blocks on this step. Build it as a per-goal setting read at surface-composition time, and make the compiler mission STATE that no design exists when it is skipped - a seat that silently gets no design cannot tell the difference between 'skipped' and 'the read failed'.

CONCURRENT EDITOR: task-f79d38b119984ae1ae51eba887a28b7d is rewriting the compiler mission sentence in agent-mission-text.ts under the owner's fence-lift ruling, and task-2c016c04dedc4eb88982a1d8d5108ddf is adding a rejection sentence to the instructions that flow into it. Expect a rebase there and do not delete either row's sentence to make yours fit.
definitionOfDone: The affordance surface offers a design step for a goal whose Gate 1 contract is APPROVED and whose decomposition has not run, and stops offering it once a design exists. Assert both transitions against a real store, and assert the step is ABSENT before Gate 1 approval - a design step offered on an unapproved contract would staff a seat with nothing to design against.

The wrapper staffs the design seat: a surface offering a READY unclaimed design step produces a spawn, asserted by work-item id. Assert its ordering relative to node.deliver is deliberate (agent-wrapper.ts:348-357 currently ranks node.deliver first) and say in a step note which rank you chose and why.

The design seat's mission reads the approved contract and the PRD and names the five sections it must submit - assert the produced mission text contains the section headings, so a seat cannot be staffed with an underspecified brief.

AFTER a design exists, the compiler mission bytes contain the design REF and the five section headings - assert on the produced mission text (the parent's DoD 2). This is the clause that makes the design load-bearing rather than decorative: a design nothing reads is a form nobody fills in twice.
Node missions cite the screens/entities they implement, drawn from the design - assert one node mission names a screen from the design it was compiled against.

THE SKIP TOGGLE: a per-goal 'plan without a design' setting makes the surface skip the design step entirely and the decomposition run opens with no design; the compiler mission STATES that no design exists rather than silently omitting it. Assert the mission text says so - the difference between 'skipped' and 'unreadable' must be visible to the seat.
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: NO UI. The Design tab, the version on the plan-approval card, the live drive and the docs are child 3's.
THE LOOP MUST NEVER BLOCK ON THIS STEP. The skip toggle is a required safety valve, not an optional extra; a goal must always be able to reach a plan.
A SKIPPED DESIGN IS STATED, NOT OMITTED. A seat that receives no design section cannot distinguish a skipped step from a failed read, and will guess.
agent-mission-text.ts has two other rows editing it concurrently (task-f79d38b1's fence-lift rewrite and task-2c016c04's rejection sentence). Rebase, do not delete their sentences.
FEATURES ONLY (inherited): no security-boundary or policy work.

implementationPlan.description: MEASURE AND VERIFY THE SEAM. NO EDITS IN THIS STEP. This row was narrowed to the WRAPPER AND MISSION third; the surface third and the skip marker are prerequisite rows and are declared in dependsOn. (a) CONFIRM THE PREREQUISITES LANDED, at the tree rather than from the board: the design step must be offered by the surface (`git grep -n 'design' apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts` and the module task-217f40b7 added) and the SKIPPED marker must be readable (`grep -n 'skip' apps/daemon/src/design/design-contracts.ts`). Read their completionSummary from get_context.epicSiblings for the exact step kind string and the marker's shape instead of re-deriving them - DO NOT invent a step kind here; the surface names it and this row consumes that name. If either is absent, moe.report_blocked with blockedOnTaskIds naming the missing row and stop. (b) CONFIRM design.submit / design.read are published (task-06ac0da1): `git grep -n 'design\.submit' -- apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` must hit. A design mission that tells a seat to call a tool no registry serves staffs a seat that can only fail. (c) MEASURE THE TWO FILE SIZES, because both are near the cap and this row's whole risk is there: `wc -l apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.ts apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-mission-text.ts` (394 and 194 at HEAD f3b94eaa). agent-wrapper.ts has SIX lines of headroom before 400. (d) RE-READ agent-mission-text.ts BEFORE PLANNING YOUR EDIT: task-f79d38b1 (fence-lift rewrite, now DONE at sha 2cd15426) and task-2c016c04 (rejection sentence) both rewrite sentences in `compilerMission`. Rebase onto whatever is there; NEVER delete another row's sentence to make yours fit.

THE DESIGN SEAT'S BRIEF. apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-mission-text.ts only. Add a `designMission(...)` beside `compilerMission` (:87) and `codeMission` (:48), following their exact shape: a `lines: string[]` built from a shared preamble plus step-specific text, joined with a single space, taking `workItemId`, `kind`, `expiresAt`, a goal ref and `projectId` and reusing `readFacts` (:41) and RETRY_ON_CONFLICT the way its siblings do. The brief must tell the seat, in this order: it holds the durable claim on the named work item until the named expiry; to call work_get_context and find the daemon's offered command; to read the APPROVED Gate 1 contract and the PRD (the same `documents_source_read` paging protocol compilerMission spells out at :95-101, including the follow-nextAlmost-until-null instruction - copy the protocol, do not paraphrase it, because a seat that pages wrong silently designs against a truncated PRD); and to submit via the offered command carrying EXACTLY the revision keys. NAME THE FIVE SECTIONS LITERALLY IN THE MISSION TEXT - `apiSurface`, `componentList`, `dataModel`, `nonFunctional`, `screens` - and say `openDecisions` is required too and may be an empty list. Import those names from `../design/design-contracts.js` (`DESIGN_SECTION_KEYS` at :44, `DESIGN_REVISION_KEYS` at :39) and interpolate them; do NOT retype the strings, or the brief and the decoder drift apart while both look right. Follow compilerMission's precedent and take NO payload-hint parameter. Add the arms to agent-mission-text.test.ts asserting the produced STRING contains each of the five headings by name, so a seat cannot be staffed with an underspecified brief.

MAKE THE DESIGN LOAD-BEARING. Same two files. This is the step that decides whether the design is real or decorative: a design nothing reads is a form nobody fills in twice. (1) `compilerMission` (:87) gains a design paragraph, driven by a new optional parameter carrying the design read's outcome (follow the existing optional-parameter style at :92-94 - `gateRef`, `instructions`, `projectId` are all `X | null = null`, so an added one keeps every existing call site compiling; that is the cheapest safe shape and it is already the file's convention). THREE OUTCOMES, and the third is the one that matters: a design EXISTS -> the mission carries its REF and the five section headings; the goal is marked SKIPPED -> the mission STATES that no design exists BECAUSE THE STEP WAS SKIPPED; no design and no marker -> say that too. A seat that simply receives no design section cannot tell 'skipped' from 'the read failed' and will guess - that is what taskRail 3 forbids. (2) `codeMission` (:48) cites the screens/entities the node implements, drawn from the design. Its `brief: NodeMission` parameter is typed in agent-wrapper.ts, so widening it touches step 4's file - decide there whether the field goes on NodeMission or is passed as its own parameter, and prefer the separate parameter, because agent-wrapper.ts has only six lines of headroom. (3) TESTS, asserting on the PRODUCED MISSION TEXT, not on a helper that rebuilds it: the compiler mission contains the design ref and all five headings when a design exists; it contains an explicit skipped statement when the marker is set; and one node mission names a screen from the design it was compiled against. Assert the skipped case by the sentence's meaning-bearing words, not by a substring so short it also matches the design-exists text.

STAFF THE SEAT. apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.ts and its test. THE FILE IS 394 LINES AND THE CAP IS 400 - measure with `wc -l` before and after every edit in this step. If your addition would cross 400, extract the inline `rank` closure at :348-351 into a tiny sibling module and import it; that REMOVES lines from this file while adding the behaviour. Do not reformat the file and do not split it otherwise. (1) The staffing loop at :339-372 already skips HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS (:352), skips `session.*` kinds (:356), dedupes by `workItemIdFor` (:358) and charges attempts only past the gate (:367). A design step offered READY and unclaimed therefore staffs ALREADY, with no change - VERIFY THAT FIRST and say so in the step note rather than adding code that was not needed. (2) What IS a decision is ORDERING. The `rank` closure at :348-351 currently ranks `node.deliver` 0, `goal.close` 2, everything else 1 - so a design step would tie with every other kind and compete with node work for the maxAgents budget. CHOOSE A RANK DELIBERATELY and write the reason in the step note: a design gates the whole decomposition behind it, so ranking it AHEAD of generic work (and still behind in-flight `node.deliver`) is the defensible default - but say which you picked and why, because DoD-2 asks for exactly that sentence. (3) Wire `designMission` into the mission dispatch so a design step gets the brief from step 2 and not the generic one. (4) TEST: a surface offering a READY unclaimed design step produces a spawn, ASSERTED BY WORK-ITEM ID (`${kind}@${aggregateId}`), not by a spawn count - a count arm passes when the wrapper staffs the wrong step. Add an ordering arm pinning the rank you chose.

DRILLS, GATES, SELF-REVIEW. (a) MUTATION DRILLS, recorded in the step note. `git status --porcelain` the exact mutated paths FIRST; all four files here are TRACKED, so an empty `git diff -- <path>` is a valid restore proof for each - state explicitly that no untracked path was mutated, so global rail 13 is answered rather than ignored, and prove each restore in a call SEPARATE from the restore. Three drills, restore and prove after each: (i) make the skipped branch of `compilerMission` fall through to the same text as the no-design branch - the DoD-6 arm must go RED, which is what proves the seat can actually tell a skip from a failed read; (ii) drop one of the five section headings from `designMission` - that heading's arm must go RED and NAME the missing heading; (iii) change the staffing rank you chose in step 4 - the ordering arm must go RED. Drill (i) is the one to run most carefully: it is the difference between this row's central promise holding and merely appearing to. (b) GATES - standalone foreground runs, one command per call, no pipes and no `;` chains, quoting the `Test Files N passed` count line for each; an exit-0 leg with NO count line ran nothing and is not evidence: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` is NOT evidence for this row and must not be quoted as such - vitest.config.ts:32 includes adapters/**, packages/**, tests/** and tools/** but no `apps/**`, so it runs zero tests against these four files. Attribute any red by failing paths at HEAD minus failing paths at merge-base, intersected with this row's four owned paths; that intersection must be EMPTY. Disclose foreign red verbatim with its failing lines; never fabricate green. Named complete_task verification command: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`. (c) ADVERSARIAL PASS on this diff only: `wc -l` both production files and confirm neither crossed 400; re-read `compilerMission` and confirm you rebased onto task-f79d38b1's and task-2c016c04's sentences rather than deleting either; a design ref that is null while the marker is also absent (the third outcome - is it stated or silently omitted?); a design whose `screens` list is empty, so a node mission has nothing to cite; two concurrent staffing passes over the same design step (the `workItemIdFor` dedupe at :358 and `staffing.has` are the guard - confirm the design step goes through them and does not bypass); a mission string built with a template literal that swallows an undefined into the text as the word 'undefined'. (d) COMPLETION RECORD must state: which staffing rank you chose and why; whether the wrapper needed any staffing change at all beyond the rank and the mission dispatch; the exact skipped-vs-absent sentences the compiler mission emits; the before/after `wc -l` for both production files; and that the surface offer and the SKIPPED marker itself are task-217f40b7's and task-365e5d97's, verified by grep at the delivered tree rather than re-implemented here.

comments.content:
NARROWED TO THE WRAPPER-AND-MISSION THIRD. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05, measured at HEAD f3b94eaa.

As claimed, this row spanned three subsystems — affordance surface, wrapper, mission text — at ~10 distinct files, with **affordance-read.ts already 468 lines (OVER the 400 cap at merge-base)** and **agent-wrapper.ts at 394 (six lines of headroom)**. Its seven DoD items were three separable deliverables. Rail 24 says split at plan time rather than let a worker find it at step 5, so:

- **task-365e5d978ba24c92a91b3ee19ab90558** (DATA axis, PLANNING, order 61.7) — the SKIPPED marker on the `design:<goalId>` aggregate.
- **task-217f40b7462e4f209ba25cb39f4acb2e** (INTERFACE axis, PLANNING, order 61.8) — the surface offers the design step and skips it when marked.
- **THIS ROW** — the wrapper staffs it and the design becomes load-bearing in all three missions. 5 steps, 4 files, plan approved.

`dependsOn` set to `[365e5d97, 217f40b7, 06ac0da1]` (previously `[5e90317e, 06ac0da1]`; 5e90317e is DONE and now covered transitively).

## THE SKIP TOGGLE WAS A HUMAN DECISION, NOT A GUESS

It had no precedent — `git grep -ln 'skipDesign|GoalSettings|perGoal' -- apps/daemon/src` = **ZERO hits** — and its obvious home was closed: `goal.create`'s payload is exact-arity `["instructions","title"]` (daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:295), so widening it is a separate multi-file roster job on the critical path. Put to the human in the REPL as three options; **they chose: record the skip as a marker on the existing design aggregate.** No new command kind, no new aggregate, no vocabulary/registry backfill. Rejected: widening `goal.create` (roster row), and a project-level flag (would have forced DoD-6 to be rewritten from per-goal to per-project). task-365e5d97 carries it, including the exact-arity hazard — `DESIGN_REVISION_KEYS` has six keys compared by arity, so a seventh redefines every existing payload's outcome.

## DoD SCOPE FOR QA — every clause is delegated by name, none narrowed

| DoD | owner |
|---|---|
| 1 — surface offers / stops offering | task-217f40b7 |
| 2 — wrapper staffs, ordering rank named | THIS row (step 4) |
| 3 — design seat mission names the five sections | THIS row (step 2) |
| 4 — compiler mission carries the design REF + headings | THIS row (step 3) |
| 5 — node missions cite screens/entities | THIS row (step 3) |
| 6 — skip toggle | SPLIT THREE WAYS: the marker = task-365e5d97; the surface skipping = task-217f40b7; **the compiler mission STATING "skipped"** = THIS row (step 3) |
| 7 — gates | THIS row (step 5) |

## MEASUREMENTS THAT CHANGED THE PLAN

1. **The wrapper already staffs a design step with no code change.** The loop at agent-wrapper.ts:339-372 filters READY/unclaimed, skips `HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS` and `session.*`, and dedupes by `workItemIdFor`. The only genuine decision is the **rank** in the inline closure at :348-351 (`node.deliver` 0, `goal.close` 2, else 1) — a design step would otherwise tie with generic work for the maxAgents budget. Step 4 tells the worker to verify this and say so rather than adding code that was not needed.
2. **`HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS` is ONE Set** at agent-spawn-contract.ts:195, re-exported by agent-wrapper.ts:24 — not duplicated. Several task descriptions on this board still claim otherwise.
3. **`ChainStep.kind` is a plain `string`**, not a closed union, so a new step kind widens no type anywhere.
4. **task-f79d38b1's fence-lift rewrite of `compilerMission` is DONE** (sha 2cd15426) and already in the file — taskRail 4 named it as an in-flight editor. task-2c016c04 may still be. Rebase; do not delete a sibling's sentence.

The row's central promise is drilled, not assumed: step 5 drill (i) collapses the skipped branch into the no-design branch and requires the DoD-6 arm to go RED — that is what proves a seat can actually tell a skip from a failed read.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
NARROWED FROM A THREE-SUBSYSTEM ROW. As claimed, this row spanned the affordance surface, the wrapper and the mission text - measured at ~10 distinct files, with affordance-read.ts ALREADY 468 lines (over the 400 cap) and agent-wrapper.ts at 394 with six lines of headroom. Its seven DoD items were three separable deliverables. Two prerequisites were filed and this row keeps the wrapper-and-mission third:
- task-365e5d978ba24c92a91b3ee19ab90558 (DATA axis) - the SKIPPED marker on the design aggregate.
- task-217f40b7462e4f209ba25cb39f4acb2e (INTERFACE axis) - the surface offers/skips the design step.
dependsOn was set to both plus task-06ac0da1 (rail 25).

THE SKIP TOGGLE'S HOME WAS A HUMAN DECISION, taken in the REPL on 2026-09-05 rather than guessed. It had NO precedent (`git grep -ln 'skipDesign|GoalSettings|perGoal' -- apps/daemon/src` = ZERO hits) and its obvious home was closed: `goal.create`'s payload is exact-arity `["instructions","title"]` (daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:295), so widening it is a separate multi-file roster job. Options put to the human: (a) a SKIPPED marker on the existing `design:<goalId>` aggregate - no new kind, no new aggregate, no roster backfill; (b) widen `goal.create` - correct-feeling but a prerequisite roster row on the critical path; (c) a project-level flag - cheapest, but would have forced DoD-6 to be rewritten from per-goal to per-project. THE HUMAN CHOSE (a). task-365e5d97 carries it.

REJECTED, keeping all three thirds in this row: the 10-file cap and two files at/over the per-file cap make it unlandable, and rail 24 says split at plan time rather than letting a worker discover it at step 5.
REJECTED, splitting the wrapper third from the mission third: they are 4 files total and the wrapper's mission dispatch and the mission text are the same change seen from two ends. Two claim/review cycles would cost more than the work.
REJECTED, putting the design's screens on the `NodeMission` type: that type lives in agent-wrapper.ts, which has six lines of headroom. A separate `codeMission` parameter costs nothing there.
REJECTED, inventing the design step's kind string in this row: the surface names it (task-217f40b7) and this row consumes that name. Two rows minting the same kind independently is how an offer and a staffer disagree while both look right.

planningNotes.risks:
FIRST - THE PER-FILE CAP, and it is tight. agent-wrapper.ts is 394 lines against a 400 cap: SIX lines of headroom for a rank change plus a mission dispatch. `wc -l` before and after each edit. The escape, if needed, is to EXTRACT the inline `rank` closure at :348-351 into a tiny sibling module - that removes lines while adding behaviour. Do not reformat and do not otherwise split the file.

SECOND - THE SKIPPED-VS-ABSENT DISTINCTION IS THIS ROW'S CENTRAL PROMISE, and it is the easiest thing to ship broken. A seat that simply receives no design section cannot tell 'the step was skipped' from 'the read failed', and will guess. compilerMission must emit THREE distinguishable outcomes, and drill (i) in step 5 - collapsing the skipped branch into the no-design branch - is what proves the arm is not vacuous. Assert on meaning-bearing words, not on a substring so short it also matches the design-exists text.

THIRD - THREE ROWS HAVE EDITED agent-mission-text.ts. task-f79d38b1's rewrite is DONE and in the file; task-2c016c04's rejection sentence may land mid-flight. Re-read the function immediately before editing and again before the final gate. Rebase; never delete a sibling's sentence to make room.

FOURTH - do not invent the design step's KIND STRING. The surface row (task-217f40b7) names it; read it from that row's delivered code. Two rows minting it independently produces an offer nothing staffs, with both sides passing their own tests.

FIFTH - assert spawns BY WORK-ITEM ID, never by count. A count arm stays green when the wrapper staffs the wrong step, which is precisely the defect the id fences.

SIXTH - a template literal that interpolates an undefined design ref writes the literal word 'undefined' into the mission a real seat then reads. Check the null paths explicitly.

SEVENTH - an empty `screens` list means a node mission has nothing to cite. Decide what the mission says then, and say it deliberately rather than emitting an empty sentence.

EIGHTH - shared checkout. Peer dirt under .moe/ and .grok/ is NEVER a stop condition: note it, never revert, stash or `git add -A`. Report every path you touch in complete_step.modifiedFiles.
